narrativeReportMd:
# VisionPrescription R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard R4-to-R6 instance-breaking change was found for local `VisionPrescription` elements: the R6 artifact keeps the same canonical identity, required R4 elements, cardinalities, shared element types, modifier behavior, and required code sets. The material local changes are optional R6 additions for request linkage and request priority, which are mostly R6-to-R4 representability and strict-parser/code-generation risks.

## Scope
The analysis is limited to the core resource definition and local terminology inputs. Inherited base-artifact changes are explicitly excluded from `findings[]` and noted as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
R4 instances can generally validate against the R6 local content model after ordinary version conversion because no existing local element was removed or tightened. R6 instances that populate `basedOn`, `groupIdentifier`, or `priority` cannot be represented natively in R4 without extensions or data loss. The new `priority` element is especially important because dropping `urgent`, `asap`, or `stat` can change request handling semantics.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issue is the R6-only `priority` element with required request-priority binding and a meaning-when-missing of normal priority. The other material issue is the addition of request lineage/grouping elements (`basedOn` and `groupIdentifier`).

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is recommended for workflows that transform R6 `priority` into R4, because the safe fallback depends on operational policy and whether urgency can be carried in an extension, order workflow artifact, or implementation-specific field.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The additions appear consistent with common FHIR request-pattern fields and were made optional, which avoids breaking existing R4 instances. A less disruptive cross-version design for R6-to-R4 exchange would require standard cross-version extensions or explicit conversion rules, not changes to the R6 resource itself.

## Follow-up analysis
Base artifact reports should own inherited Element/DomainResource changes. SearchParameter reports should assess API-level changes such as the R6 `VisionPrescription-product` search parameter.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard R4-to-R6 validation break was found for `VisionPrescription`. The main migration concerns are R6-only request linkage (`basedOn`, `groupIdentifier`), R6-only urgency (`priority`), and lossless R6-to-R4 conversion. Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition differences but lower for rationale because official diff/narrative pages were not available locally.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration from R4 to R6 is structurally straightforward for existing local elements: no required R4 field was removed, no shared cardinality was tightened, and no shared type or reference target was narrowed. Migration from R6 back to R4 needs explicit handling for new optional request-pattern fields. `priority` should not be silently dropped when it carries `urgent`, `asap`, or `stat`; `basedOn` and `groupIdentifier` should be preserved through extensions, companion artifacts, or documented loss if round-tripping matters.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, types, flags, and bindings because the local R4/R6 StructureDefinitions and local CodeSystems were compared directly. Confidence is medium for design intent and prevalence because official narrative diffs and real-world usage data were not available. Terminology confidence is high for the required local code systems inspected, but formal ValueSet expansions were not present.

findings.title: R6 adds request linkage and grouping elements

oldState.summary: R4 has no `basedOn` or `groupIdentifier` elements on VisionPrescription.
oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 `VisionPrescription` can identify the prescription itself through `identifier`, but it has no native fields for the request or plan fulfilled by the prescription and no composite/group identifier for multiple simultaneously authorized prescriptions.

semanticText.short: What prescription fulfills; Composite request identifier
semanticText.definition: `basedOn`: Plan/proposal/order/request fulfilled by this prescription. `groupIdentifier`: A shared identifier common to all Vision Prescriptions authorized more or less simultaneously by a single author.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 aligns `VisionPrescription` with request-pattern metadata by allowing it to point back to a fulfilled plan/order/request and to share a group identifier across related prescriptions.

facts.note: R6-only summary element for request/plan lineage.
R6-only summary element for composite request grouping.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are new element ids in the R6 differential and snapshot with no corresponding R4 `VisionPrescription` element names or nearby renamed fields.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because both fields are optional, an R4 instance that omits them is not invalidated by R6. The risk appears when an R6 instance contains them: a strict R4 parser or validator will reject the unknown elements, while a tolerant transformer that drops them loses request lineage and grouping information.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The added fields do not change the lens prescription values themselves, but loss of request provenance or grouping can affect order reconciliation, audit, and fulfillment workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Align VisionPrescription with common FHIR request-pattern fields for provenance and grouped ordering.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because the R6 elements are optional additions that preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--adding first-class request lineage and grouped-order metadata to `VisionPrescription`--is reasonable and was implemented as optional R6 content. That does not invalidate R4 instances migrating forward, so the remaining compatibility issue is older R4 systems receiving newer R6 content. Under the calibration rules, that makes the backward-compatible alternative question not applicable rather than `Partial`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because `basedOn` and `groupIdentifier` are optional. Cross-version extensions, companion artifacts, or audit sidecars may preserve these values when converting R6 data back to R4, but those are migration mitigations. Avoiding the R6 elements entirely would preserve older parser compatibility but would fail the R6 goal of native request-pattern support.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 extensions or sidecars can mitigate down-conversion loss, but they are not less-breaking base R6 designs.

evidence.detail: No R4 differential or snapshot element id exists for `VisionPrescription.basedOn` or `VisionPrescription.groupIdentifier`.
R6 defines `basedOn` as 0..* Reference to CarePlan, RequestOrchestration, NutritionOrder, or ServiceRequest.

evidence.quote: A shared identifier common to all Vision Prescriptions that were authorized more or less simultaneously by a single author.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example is illustrative and includes the minimum surrounding required VisionPrescription fields needed to show where the R6-only elements appear. The extension URLs shown are illustrative placeholders for a cross-version strategy; implementers should use official cross-version extensions or local IG-defined extensions if available.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds native request lineage and grouping to `VisionPrescription`. This is not a hard R4-to-R6 validation break because existing R4 data can omit both fields, but it is a real migration concern for systems that must accept R6 data with R4 validators, generated R4 classes, database schemas, or FHIRPath expressions that assume the R4 shape.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance does not become invalid merely because R6 adds optional fields. A valid R6 instance containing `basedOn` or `groupIdentifier`, however, is not valid as an R4 `VisionPrescription` without extensions or data removal. Generated R4 models will usually have no properties for these fields, and strict JSON/XML validation against R4 will reject them as unknown elements.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: R4-to-R6 transforms can leave these fields absent unless request lineage is available elsewhere. R6-to-R4 transforms should decide whether to preserve them in official cross-version extensions, local extensions, companion resources, or an audit sidecar. Test conversions with multiple `basedOn` references and a populated `groupIdentifier` so silent data loss is detected.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 design is additive and optional, so it is backward-compatible for R4 instances moving forward. Native R4 round-trip compatibility could only be preserved by avoiding the new elements or standardizing extensions for R4; that alternative keeps older parsers happy but sacrifices first-class request-pattern semantics in R6.

findings.title: R6 adds request priority with required priority codes

oldState.narrativeMd: Any priority or urgency for an R4 vision prescription had to be represented outside the base resource, for example in workflow context, extensions, notes, or implementation-specific conventions.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `priority` as 0..1 code with required binding to request-priority.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R6 CodeSystem contains `routine`, `urgent`, `asap`, and `stat`. The ValueSet has no embedded expansion in the package, so the codes were read from the included local CodeSystem.

semanticText.definition: Indicates how quickly the vision prescription should be addressed with respect to other requests.
semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: If missing, this request should be performed with normal priority.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 gives `VisionPrescription` a first-class urgency field and defines a normal-priority default when it is absent.

facts.newValue: If missing, this request should be performed with normal priority.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `VisionPrescription.priority` appears only in the R6 differential and snapshot. No R4 local element has equivalent path, name, or request-priority binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The new field is optional, so R4 instances are not made invalid in R6. The high R6-to-R4 risk comes from semantics: an R6 `stat`, `asap`, or `urgent` priority has no native R4 destination, and silently dropping it can alter fulfillment order or safety-sensitive workflow behavior. Runtime/codegen risk is medium because R6 models and enum handling gain a new property that R4 models lack.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Priority can influence timeliness of fulfillment. Losing an explicit `stat`, `asap`, or `urgent` value during R6-to-R4 conversion can create clinically or operationally meaningful misprioritization.

justification.inferredGoal: Expose standard request priority directly on VisionPrescription.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because optional R6 `priority` does not make R4-valid instances invalid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--adding a standard urgency signal aligned with request priority--is reasonable, and the R6 design is optional with a required binding only when the element is present. Existing R4 instances can omit `priority` and remain structurally compatible moving forward. The serious risk is lossy R6-to-R4 down-conversion of urgent/asap/stat values, so the calibrated availability is `Not applicable` rather than a base-design `Partial` alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no applicable less-breaking base R6 alternative for preserving R4-to-R6 validity because the added element is optional. A standardized cross-version extension, ConceptMap-backed transform, or workflow-side preservation rule can reduce R6-to-R4 data loss, but those are exchange mitigations outside the base R6 resource design. Not adding `priority` would avoid older-schema rejection but would also omit the native R6 urgency semantics.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Extensions or conversion rules help R6-to-R4 exchange, but they are mitigations and do not replace a base R6 alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `priority` as 0..1 `code`, required binding to `ValueSet/request-priority|6.0.0-ballot4`, and summary element.
The local R6 request-priority CodeSystem defines `routine`, `urgent`, `asap`, and `stat`.

examples.examplesMd: The example focuses on the R6-only `priority` value. An R4 base `VisionPrescription` has no native place for this property, so the migration example shows the kind of extension-based preservation a cross-version transform would need.

findings.narrativeMd: `VisionPrescription.priority` is a new R6 local element. It does not make existing R4 instances invalid, but it gives R6 instances a new urgency signal that older R4 schemas and generated models do not understand. This is more than cosmetic because the element's meaning-when-missing states that absence means normal priority.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken by the addition. R6-to-R4 validation is affected whenever `priority` is present: a strict R4 validator rejects the unknown element, and a lossy transform that drops it changes `urgent`, `asap`, or `stat` into an implicit normal-priority request. R6 validators also enforce the required value set when the field is present.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, populate `priority` only when reliable urgency data exists; otherwise omission has normal-priority semantics in R6. For R6-to-R4, do not silently drop non-routine priority. Preserve it in an official cross-version extension or local extension, route it through an associated request/order artifact, or flag the instance for manual review. Test all four codes and a missing-priority case.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The optional R6 field is a reasonable additive design. The remaining compatibility problem is inherent to sending newer content to older R4 systems. A standard cross-version extension would be the most backward-compatible mitigation, but it depends on transformer and consumer support.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, `DomainResource` base, and abstract flag are unchanged. Metadata maturity/status changed and is captured as a notable non-breaking change.
No local R4 element was removed, renamed, split, or moved. The only local presence changes found are optional R6 additions reported in `findings[]`.

All shared local element min/max cardinalities are unchanged, including required fields such as `status`, `created`, `patient`, `dateWritten`, `prescriber`, `lensSpecification`, `lensSpecification.product`, `lensSpecification.eye`, and prism sub-elements.
All shared local element datatypes are unchanged. No R4 choice type was removed or narrowed because `VisionPrescription` has no local choice element in the compared differential.

Shared local reference targets are unchanged: `patient` remains `Patient`, `encounter` remains `Encounter`, and `prescriber` remains `Practitioner | PractitionerRole`. New `basedOn` targets are covered in a finding.

Existing required bindings still point to the same logical ValueSets with version updates: `fm-status`, `vision-eye-codes`, and `vision-base-codes`. The local CodeSystems have the same code lists across R4 and R6. Formal expansions were not embedded in the ValueSet resources.

No VisionPrescription-owned differential constraints or invariants were found in either version. Snapshot constraint differences observed for generic element/domain-resource rules are inherited and out of scope for this report.
No local fixed values, patterns, or defaults were added, removed, or changed on shared elements.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex constraint changes were found on shared elements.

`VisionPrescription.status` remains the only local modifier element, and its modifier rationale is unchanged. R6 explicitly writes `isModifier: false` for many elements where R4 omitted the false value; that is not a semantic modifier change.
Effective summary flags for shared local elements are unchanged. The R6-only additions are summary elements and are reported separately.
No local slicing was present or changed in the compared VisionPrescription definitions.
No shared local element changed its JSON/XML representation, name, or choice suffix. Serialization risk is limited to the new R6 element names, which older R4 parsers will not recognize.

The only local R6-to-R4 representability gaps found are the R6-only `basedOn`, `groupIdentifier`, and `priority` elements. The rest of the shared local content model remains representable at the StructureDefinition level.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact maturity and ownership metadata changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The resource canonical identity and structural base did not change. The metadata changed from R4 draft/trial-use/FMM 2 with Financial Management ownership to R6 active/normative/FMM 3 with Orders and Observations ownership. This affects governance and expectations, not instance validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementation roadmaps and conformance documentation may need to update maturity/status references, especially if local policy treats normative resources differently from trial-use resources.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records false modifier/summary flags in the differential
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 often omitted `isModifier: false` or `isSummary: false`; R6 explicitly records false values on many local differential elements. The effective meaning is unchanged: the only local modifier remains `status`, and shared summary membership is unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Schema diff tooling should normalize absent false values to `false` to avoid noisy false positives.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Eye-code comment wording was clarified
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The `lensSpecification.eye` definition, cardinality, type, required code values, and binding strength are unchanged. R6 only revises the comment text, including correcting the Latin spelling for left eye from `siniter` to `sinister` and mentioning paper claim forms/medical records.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and generated comments may differ, but validators and instance data are unaffected.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Existing required bindings point to R6 versions with unchanged local code sets
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The value set references changed from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`, but the local CodeSystems inspected for `fm-status`, `vision-eye-codes`, and `vision-base-codes` contain the same codes and definitions. No code removal or required-binding strengthening was found for shared elements.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Version-sensitive validators should use the R6 value set versions when validating R6, but code-level migrations are not indicated for these existing elements.
